definition: The Language Grid (Japanese: 言語グリッド, Hepburn: Gengo Guriddo) is an online multilingual service platform developed in Japan.
details: It integrates language resources such as dictionaries, bilingual corpora, and machine translation systems using web service technologies, and users combine them to configure customized multilingual environments. Its operation started in 2007 as a research project centered on the National Institute of Information and Communications Technology (NICT) and Kyoto University, and after developing into an international network, the operating body was transferred to the NPO Language Grid Association in 2017. This project received the Institute of Electronics, Information and Communication Engineers (IEICE) Achievement Award in 2012, and its service-oriented design architecture is adopted by projects such as the LAPPS Grid in the U.S. and the European Language Grid in Europe.

explainer.lead: The Language Grid is an online multilingual service platform developed in Japan that combines language resources so users can configure customized multilingual environments. It matters as shared infrastructure rather than a single tool.

tiers.eli5: It's like an app store of language tools — dictionaries, translation engines, text collections — that you snap together into the setup you need.
tiers.practitioner: Users integrate dictionaries, bilingual corpora and machine translation systems through web service technologies to assemble a custom environment. The pitfall is that composed services inherit the quality limits of each component.

explainer.example: A user combines a dictionary service and a machine translation service into one multilingual environment for their community.
